items.t: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels
items.d: Daytona is building a cloud for agents that's like giving every agent its own computer. It has attracted founders of Stripe, Perplextity, Datadog, Mercor, and others as angels, it says.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 9:26 AM PDT · October 23, 2026 Image Credits: Daytona / CEO Ivan Burazin flanked by chief architect Goran Draganić (left) and CTO Vedran Jukic Julie Bort Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million. The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants. Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round . Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform. AI 기사요약 다음주 국내외 증시는 미국 FOMC의 기준금리 결정과 주요 경제지표 발표, 글로벌 빅테크 및 국내 반도체 기업들의 실적 공개를 통해 AI 투자 수익성과 통화정책 방향성을 검증하며 방향성을 모색할 전망입니다. 美 FOMC·물가지표·GDP 발표 줄줄이…금리 경로 재평가 삼성전자·SK하이닉스 실적 공개…HBM 호황 지속 여부 주목 MS·알파벳·아마존 AI 투자 성적표…BOJ 결정도 변수 로이터연합뉴스 다음주 국내외 증시는 미국 중앙은행(Fed)의 기준금리 결정과 주요 빅테크 기업의 실적 발표에 따라 방향을 모색할 전망이다. 미국에서는 27~28일(현지시간) 연방공개시장위원회(FOMC)가 열리고 마이크로소프트(MS)와 알파벳, 아마존 등 대형 기술기업이 잇달아 실적을 공개한다. 국내에서는 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 3분기 실적 발표가 예정돼 있다. 최근 증시를 흔든 미국발 물가 부담과 인공지능(AI) 투자 수익성 논란이 실제 경제지표와 기업 실적을 통해 검증받는 한 주가 될 전망이다. 관건은 빅테크의 이익과 현금흐름 증가가 막대한 AI 투자비용을 뒷받침할 수 있는지다. 미국 빅테크의 설비투자 전망은 국내 반도체 기업의 향후 실적을 가늠할 핵심 변수다. 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임은 사용자에게 있습니다. 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 전예진 기자 기사댓글 개의 댓글이 있습니다. 댓글 닫기

Oura sues rival Ultrahuman again, threatening its US smart ring comeback
items.d: Oura alleges in its newest lawsuit that Ultrahuman's Ring Pro infringes two of its patents.
items.fullText: Smart ring maker Oura has sued Indian rival Ultrahuman again, seeking to block U.S. sales of its Ring Pro (pictured above) just months after the redesign helped the Bengaluru-based startup return to the American market following an import ban. The case is the latest in a string of patent disputes Oura has brought against competing smart ring makers, including Samsung and RingConn. In a complaint filed Thursday in a federal court in Texas, Oura alleged that Ultrahuman’s Ring Pro infringes two of its patents covering the ring’s design and internal components, including its battery and sensors. Oura is seeking monetary damages and a permanent injunction that would stop Ultrahuman from selling the ring. Ultrahuman’s redesigned Ring Pro, launched in February, received a favorable ruling from U.S. Customs and Border Protection in March, paving the way for the startup’s return to the U.S. market . The decision followed an import ban on Ultrahuman’s earlier Ring Air, which took effect after Oura secured a patent infringement ruling from the International Trade Commission in August last year. “Ultrahuman has a history of copying Oura’s innovations, as demonstrated by the 2025 ITC ruling against the company,” an Oura spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “Ultrahuman introduced a redesigned ring but failed to address continued infringement of Oura’s patents, seeking instead to capitalize on our innovation and the market leadership we have built.” Oura argues that the Customs ruling covered only the patent involved in the earlier dispute, not the two patents cited in its latest lawsuit: D804,471 and 12,769,363. “To protect its patent rights, Oura is now forced to file this complaint of patent infringement,” the company said in its filing. Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis
items.d: There were few, if any, reports of widespread damage by hackers exploiting PHP flaws, experts said, one day after officials warned of severe vulnerabilities.
items.fullText: Security Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis The vulnerabilities are devastating in theory. But experts say they are also technically very difficult to hack. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 After researchers quietly found two devastating software vulnerabilities in August, they worked across borders and disciplines to develop patches that were released to the world Wednesday morning. Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 22, 2026, 6:07 PM EDT By Kevin Collier One day after governments around the world warned that newly publicized software vulnerabilities were so severe that websites should consider going offline until they could fix them, experts and insiders said there are few, if any, reports of widespread damage. That could still change, of course, and cybersecurity experts warn that the threat will remain for weeks, if not longer. Still, there were early signs Thursday that hackers were finding it difficult to capitalize on the vulnerabilities. “Across all our telemetry, and we are looking hard, we have only seen a couple of real exploitation attempts,” said Don Smith, vice president of threat research at the British software security firm Sophos. Experts agree that that was in part because of a behind-the-scenes, global effort that identified the flaw and quietly designed a fix to address it. The effort was aided, inadvertently, by the current limits of some widely available AI models, which did not appear to be very helpful at exploiting the vulnerabilities. And perhaps, they said, a little bit of luck. “My sense is that these [vulnerabilities] are harder to exploit than folks thought at first, so this could be a slow burn,” Smith said. The flaws were in PHP, a website programming language that is used in an estimated 69% of all websites. General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence.
